# `⍋` — Grade up / Grade up by

Function. Keys: `Alt-Backslash 7`. Hanzi: `升`. Ranks: `∞` monadic, `∞ ∞` dyadic

`⍋Y` gives indices that sort major cells ascending. Stable; uses [structural ordering](../evaluation.qmd#equality-and-ordering), without tolerance.

```bpl
⍋30 10 20          ⍝ [1 2 0]ₓ
v←30 10 20 ⋄ [⍋v]⌷v ⍝ 10 20 30
⍋2 1 2 1           ⍝ [1 3 0 2]ₓ
```

The positions keep the name of `Y`'s first axis. Selecting with a grade along axis `i` sorts each column of a matrix with axes `i` and `j`:

```bpl
x←["i":3 "j":4]⍴3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6 5 3 5 8
x.[(⍋⍠"i" x)]      ⍝ ["i":3 "j":4]⍴[3 1 2 1⋄5 3 4 6⋄5 9 5 8]
```

`C⍋Y` uses a character collation array `C`.

```bpl
"cba"⍋"abc"        ⍝ [2 1 0]ₓ
```

See [`⍒`](del-stile.qmd), and [`<`](less-than.qmd) to sort.

## Fast combinations

These trains and compositions give the result of applying their parts in turn, faster. [Trains](../evaluation.qmd#trains) says which spellings BPL recognises.

| Combination | Applies to | Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| `k↑⍋ Y` or `(k↑)∘⍋` | a vector of reals or characters without keys, with the count at most a quarter of its length | selects the first `k` positions of the grade, or the last `-k`, without ordering the rest |
| `↑⍋ Y`, `i⌷⍋ Y` or `i⊃⍋ Y` | the same vectors | selects one position without ordering the rest |
| `⍋⍋ Y` or `⍋∘⍋` | any `Y` without keys on its first axis | gives each major cell's rank by inverting the first grade, without grading it again |

```bpl
v←30 10 20 50 40 60 70 80 90 0
2↑⍋ v                                ⍝ [9 1]ₓ
⍋⍋ v                                 ⍝ [3 1 2 5 4 6 7 8 9 0]ₓ
(•explain "2↑⍋ v").fast.combination  ⍝ ["partial grade"]
```

## Inverse

`⍋⁻¹P` gives an array whose grade is the permutation `P`. Any other `P` is a `DOMAIN` error.

```bpl
⍋⁻¹2 0 1   ⍝ [1 2 0]ₓ
```
